chunks: Zakariyya ibn Adam asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about shortening.

Concerning how much distance a man shortens for when he is in the landed properties of his household, and his authority is valid in them, traveling through the properties for two days and two nights, or three days and their nights.
So he wrote: "Shortening applies in the journey of one day and one night."

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: the members of his household or family
key_terms.مَسِيرَةِ: the extent or duration of a journey
key_terms.يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ: one day and one night, indicating the travel measure mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: When does shortening the salat (prayer) apply while traveling through one's family lands?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling of qaṣr during travel, specifically for a person moving through lands belonging to his family over which he has authority. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that shortening the salat (prayer) applies for the journey of one day and one night.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1304 - Zakariyya ibn Adam asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (as) about the distance for shortening prayers when a man is in the lands belonging to his family and has control over them, traveling through these lands for two days and two nights or three days and their nights.
Abu al-Hasan (as) wrote in response, "Shortening is applicable for the journey of one day and one night."
